results.title: The “Bronze Age” of Southern Africa: Insights from Isotopes and ...
results.content: This is an abstract from the "Archaeological Science and African Archaeology: Appreciating the Impact of David Killick" session, at the 88th annual meeting of the Society for American Archaeology. The Southern Africa project (2015–present) uses lead and tin isotopes plus trace element concentrations to infer the geological provenance of copper and tin in Iron Age copper alloys, and to investigate the behaviors responsible for moving these objects from their geological source to the eventual site of deposition. Earlier archaeometallurgical work established the presence of bronze at large sites in southern Africa, but a recent project hinted at its presence at non-elite sites as well. This presentation will summarize isotopic and chemical data from bronze samples and assess temporal and spatial patterns in alloying practice and tin source for a material that we now know was much more widely produced than previously realized. Presented at The 88th Annual Meeting of the Society for American Archaeology.
